title: Target validity
requirement: Every decision rejects dead, destroyed, invalid, out-of-arena or otherwise non-targetable actors.
behavior: Morgott engages a valid opponent and stops offensive behavior at encounter termination. How his internal target-object validity and leash checks are encoded is unknown.
design: Before every neutral or follow-up decision, reject dead/destroyed/non-targetable or off-arena targets; abandon an attack gracefully when a target becomes invalid.
verify: Kill/despawn the player, break encounter boundaries and interrupt a queued follow-up; expect safe reacquisition/reset.

title: Gate-time snapshot
requirement: A timestamped combat context is rebuilt atomically at every neutral, combo or reaction gate.
behavior: Morgott visibly changes follow-ups based on where the player finishes a dodge, suggesting fresh situation evaluation, but no public proof establishes atomic snapshots or timestamps.
design: At every neutral, combo or reaction gate capture target location, action tags, facing, distance, LOS, boss phase and clock time in one immutable FCombatContext.
verify: Move behind Morgott during one combo; debug logs must show a fresh gate snapshot and the corresponding branch.

title: Distance convention
requirement: Each attack declares whether range means root, capsule-surface or attack-origin distance.
behavior: The spear has long reach, dagger pressure is strongest up close, and the sword/hammer cover different extents; exact range measurement convention is not published.
design: Document root-to-root versus capsule edge versus attack-origin distance in each MoveData; avoid inconsistent range checks between selectors and traces.
verify: Place target on min/max range thresholds and repeat from different capsule sizes; compare eligibility with actual reach.

title: Signed angle and hysteresis
requirement: Relative yaw is planar, boss-facing and stable near sector boundaries.
behavior: Tail swipes answer positions behind him, and frontal or flank positioning changes certain sword/hammer continuations in detailed player observations.
design: Compute signed planar target yaw relative to boss forward; add enter/leave thresholds around rear and side sectors to prevent flicker.
verify: Orbit across front/side/rear boundaries while an attack finishes; verify stable branch selection without oscillation.

title: Vertical separation
requirement: Melee and ground actions enforce a documented Z tolerance.
behavior: The fight mostly takes place on a relatively flat arena; no evidence establishes Morgott’s internal Z-difference gates.
design: Apply vertical tolerance to sword, hammer, ground shockwaves and spear charge; define airborne exceptions for projectiles and leap attacks.
verify: Raise the player on test platforms; verify no ground sweep or melee attack hits vertically impossible targets.

title: Observable player activity
requirement: Reactions use public committed action state, not raw future input.
behavior: Players report Morgott responding to committed healing, long casts, and guard-break states; this should not be interpreted as knowledge of future button presses.
design: Expose player action tags only after the animation/ability actually starts; gate reaction by commitment, LOS, feasible distance and reaction delay.
verify: Heal inside and outside reach; cancel during startup; ensure reaction never fires on input before an action is visible.

title: LOS and memory
requirement: Precision reactions require current LOS; lost targets use timestamped last-seen state and reacquire.
behavior: The arena is open and line-of-sight is generally unobstructed, but last-seen timers and LOS handling are not documented.
design: Require current LOS for precision throws; store last-seen position/time and use a reacquire or search fallback after LOS loss.
verify: Introduce an occluding temporary wall and loss/reacquisition conditions; verify response is not omniscient.

title: Soft adaptation memory
requirement: Pattern features decay, are capped and bias rather than force choices.
behavior: Repeated-position pressure may result from fixed positional rules; evidence does not establish a decaying memory or player-pattern model.
design: If adaptation is desired, track short-lived capped recent heal/roll/rear-camping metrics; bias preferences rather than guarantee a hard counter.
verify: Repeat backward rolls then vary behavior; ensure reactions shift probabilistically and decay after the pattern stops.

title: Legal decision gates
requirement: Full attack selection runs only in neutral or an explicitly authorized gate.
behavior: Morgott’s attacks visibly commit and branch rather than instantly switching on every player movement; the exact internal selection-gate topology is unknown.
design: Call selection in neutral or authored combo/reaction windows only; keep active committed motion under a single executor.
verify: Move player rapidly during active attack; ensure no illegal attack change until the next legal gate.

title: Hard-filter precedence
requirement: Phase, state, range, angle, LOS, cooldown, resource, asset and path constraints reject before scoring.
behavior: His weapon choices are context-sensitive: dagger at closer spacing, spear throws at range, tail response from behind, and health-gated moves.
design: Hard-filter by phase, state, attack range, angle, LOS, cooldown and asset readiness; score only passing candidates.
verify: At each position/phase enumerate rejected candidates and reasons; no impossible move should be selected.

title: Executable asset gate
requirement: A move with a missing montage/socket/required resource is never selected.
behavior: The shipped boss of course has working animations; a data/asset validity gate inside FromSoftware’s runtime is not observable.
design: Validate montage, sockets, curves, reaction ability and VFX references during content audit and at runtime before committing.
verify: Delete an attack montage reference in a dev copy; attack should be skipped with diagnostics, not leave boss frozen.

title: Normalized utility
requirement: Eligible moves receive comparable documented range, angle, opportunity, spacing, phase and variety terms.
behavior: Morgott creates the impression of contextual selection, but neither a utility-scoring equation nor its weights are established publicly.
design: Use normalized scores for geometry, target commitment, phase, spacing, combo intent, variety and hazards; tune from recorded fights.
verify: Replay identical contexts with debug scoring; highest eligible utility should dominate without deterministic repetition.

title: Bounded randomness
requirement: Variation is limited to near-best candidates, with deterministic seeded RNG.
behavior: Different choices occur in comparable situations, but we cannot verify seeded RNG, near-best sampling, or exact randomness limits.
design: Randomly choose among near-best legal attacks with reproducible local seed for tests; keep deterministic cooldown and rule enforcement.
verify: Run 1000 seeded neutral gates; confirm diversity, no invalid moves, and reproducible outputs.

title: Cooldown semantics
requirement: Cooldown commits on an attack start, not on rejected or failed choice attempts.
behavior: Community moveset analysis identifies attack-specific cooldown behavior, but not the engine’s precise commit semantics.
design: Start cooldown only when the montage successfully enters the committed attack; failed selection or montage playback must not consume it.
verify: Force montage-start failure then retry; confirm cooldown was not consumed.

title: Anti-repeat memory
requirement: Recent move and family repetition lower preference with time decay; hard spacing may protect signature moves.
behavior: The moveset contains numerous attacks and reported cooldowns, but explicit anti-repeat memory and decay are not publicly verified.
design: Add recent attack-family penalties and optional minimum separation for signature rain/hammer spins; store expiring history on committed starts.
verify: Fight at one fixed range for 5 minutes; histogram short-loop repeats and long-form variety.

title: No-candidate fallback
requirement: Empty eligible sets choose purposeful wait, reorientation, approach/retreat, EQS positioning or reset.
behavior: Morgott uses idle, approach, hops, and repositioning between attacks; no-candidate implementation is not disclosed.
design: If no attack is eligible, intentionally face, approach, retreat, strafe, reset, or search, with bounded durations; never spin in a retry loop.
verify: Disable all valid attacks; watch boss choose visible purposeful neutral action without CPU spikes.

title: Reaction latency and budget
requirement: Defensive/heal reactions require nonzero latency, cooldown/budget and ordinary feasibility.
behavior: A flask or cast may invite quick projectiles and gap closing, but exact reaction latency or budget cannot be established by observation alone.
design: Add nonzero reaction latency, cooldown, animation free-state, LOS and travel-time rules; never interrupt committed motion to cheat.
verify: Use healing at several ranges and just after attack commit; measure realistic response latency and valid interruptions.

title: Decision trace
requirement: Each gate logs context, all candidate eligibility/reasons/scores, winner and RNG seed.
behavior: No public view exposes Morgott’s internal attack scoring trace or seed values.
design: Log gate ID, player state, all filtered candidates and reasons, selected move, RNG seed and phase in a development-only ring buffer.
verify: Recreate any test run from trace and seed; compare selected sequence to recorded animation events.

title: Single execution authority
requirement: One executor owns current attack, instance, section, state, target snapshot and victim sets.
behavior: Only one coherent attack appears to own each active weapon/action, but internal executor ownership is unknown.
design: Use one UBossAttackExecutorComponent as authority for attack instance, montage/section, phase, victim records, hit windows and cleanup.
verify: Trigger combo, stagger and phase transition on the same frame; one authoritative final state remains.

title: Instance before montage
requirement: A unique ID and wind-up state are set before montage playback.
behavior: There is no public evidence of Morgott’s internal attack instance creation order.
design: Create unique FAttackInstanceId and set wind-up state before Montage_Play and Notify activation; carry ID through effects and damage.
verify: Add immediate startup notify and forced montage failure; verify events map to the correct instance.

title: Start rollback
requirement: Montage play failure restores neutral/movement and does not consume a live attack.
behavior: Montage startup rollback is a hidden engine implementation detail.
design: Check playback handle; on failure atomically reset movement/rotation/temporary states and do not consume attack cooldown.
verify: Provide missing Montage in a test Data Asset; boss resumes neutral and chooses a fallback.

title: Stale event rejection
requirement: Notify/callback instance, montage, section and expected state are validated.
behavior: Stale animation callback rejection is not externally observable.
design: Every callback validates instance ID, montage, section and expected state; reject old timelines after interruption or phase change.
verify: Interrupt and immediately start a new attack; late Notify must not damage or trigger an old branch.

title: Explicit priority
requirement: Death, phase, stance, special, combo and completion conflicts follow a documented order.
behavior: Morgott can be staggered and phase-transition mid-fight; these are visible priorities, though the exact arbitration table is unknown.
design: Declare priority: death > forced phase > stance break > unavoidable transition > attack abort > legal combo > recovery, with design exceptions.
verify: Hit stance threshold as phase threshold is crossed; verify a single valid transition and no overlapping offense.

title: Idempotent abort
requirement: Abort closes collision, warping, gates, armor and latent work, then restores motion once.
behavior: Disappearing active attacks after stagger/death imply cleanup, but idempotent abort internals are hidden.
design: Abort exactly once: stop traces, cancel spawned persistent actors when required, release warp, clear armor and reset gate state.
verify: Call Abort twice during active grab/AoE; expect no extra hit or leaked animation state.

title: Watchdog
requirement: Every live attack has maximum expected duration plus margin and a safe timeout path.
behavior: No public information documents an attack watchdog or duration margin.
design: Track max expected montage duration plus bounded margin; if state is still live, close damage and transition to safe recovery.
verify: Suppress Montage End/Notify End in a controlled dev test; verify no permanent attack lock.

title: Cleanup-before-unlock
requirement: Trace and temporary state are closed before any next selection can occur.
behavior: It cannot be established whether hit volumes are torn down before the next selection gate internally.
design: Close active attack collision and temporary invulnerability/warp state before clearing busy flag or choosing follow-up.
verify: Spam branching and interrupt at edge frames; no hit from a previous attack may land after next start.

title: Authored graph
requirement: Combo nodes and allowed outgoing edges are data-authored, not arbitrary full-pool selections.
behavior: Community flowcharts document opening moves and restricted follow-up families: e.g. spear charge can lead to different sword/hammer continuations depending on position.
design: Author move nodes, legal next-edge lists, gate timing, hit/guard/whiff prerequisites and cooldowns as Data Assets.
verify: Render attack graph from assets; all observed branches must appear; no unrelated attack may enter a combo gate.

title: Gate after damage
requirement: A branch gate occurs only at its authored time, normally after the prior hit window closes.
behavior: Many follow-ups occur after a slash, charge or slam has reached a recognizable completed-hit stage; exact internal event marker is undisclosed.
design: Place combo-gate Notifies after active hit window closes, unless move card explicitly allows overlapping multi-weapon hits.
verify: Slow animation to 0.25x; prove hitbox closes before branch gate for representative combos.

title: Fresh branch context
requirement: The gate evaluates current target state, not only the first move's snapshot.
behavior: Changing position during a spear charge or dodge can alter whether a frontal sword continuation or an angled hammer response follows.
design: At each gate resample player range/yaw/action; never reuse only the initiating attack snapshot.
verify: Dodge behind vs remain in front during spear charge; record two different eligible follow-up families.

title: Explicit hit-confirm policy
requirement: Each edge states whether contact, damage, guard or whiff is required.
behavior: Reported guard-break interactions can change Morgott’s follow-up behavior; source notes some equipment-dependent exceptions.
design: Every edge declares hit confirm / blocked / guard-broken / whiff / location conditions; separate confirmed hit from raw overlap.
verify: Compare clean whiff, guarded strike, parry and guard break; follow-up branches must match configured conditions.

title: Single-use gate
requirement: A gate is consumed once per matching instance.
behavior: Repeated follow-up transition callbacks cannot be inspected externally.
design: Consume a combo gate exactly once per attack instance and gate ID, even if Notify fires twice or the montage scrubs.
verify: Emit duplicate gate events and validate only one follow-up is committed.

title: Finite pressure
requirement: Combo depth, edge use/cooldown and maximum pressure duration enforce eventual recovery.
behavior: He has long multi-weapon strings but also finishers such as the spinning sword/hammer sequence, allowing counterattacks after the sequence ends.
design: Bound graph depth, number of repeat edges and pressure time; finishers always reach recovery unless special scripted phase behavior intervenes.
verify: Force max-depth combos in 100 fights; none should loop forever or prevent all offense from the player.

title: Default recovery
requirement: A missing/invalid target, edge or montage routes to declared recovery.
behavior: When the player escapes range, Morgott may end a sequence, hop away, or reacquire rather than continuing every attack without a target.
design: Missing edge/invalid target/failed Montage resolves to an authored recovery pose and intentional neutral movement.
verify: Remove target during gate; verify no frozen animation or instantaneous neutral bypass.

title: Montage timeline authority
requirement: Commit, active, gate, armor and recovery derive from montage events/position rather than duplicate delays.
behavior: Weapon release and impact visibly follow authored animation; exact animation-notify pipeline and engine event authority are not public.
design: Drive attack hit windows, commit points, warp permissions and recovery transitions from Montage Notifies and montage-position checks; avoid unrelated timers.
verify: Play at 0.5x and during hitches; hit events should follow authored frame positions.

title: Telegraph phases
requirement: Pose/direction/release cues precede damage and identify geometry.
behavior: Morgott uses readable wind-ups, summoned holy weapon silhouettes, sword rain setup, and bloodflame infusion cues before distinctive attacks.
design: Build attack telegraph design per move: pose, left/right weapon, floor cue, audio onset, release cue, camera framing and active hit shape.
verify: Blindplay tester identifies thrust/sweep/hammer/rain/grab from their cues without looking at debug labels.

title: Bounded holds
requirement: Variable delay has declared min/max and is chosen before commitment with a reliable release cue.
behavior: Delayed sword/hammer releases are perceptible, but precise variable random hold durations are not proven.
design: If adding variable hold, define min/max chosen at wind-up start and make release animation readable; do not assume Morgott randomizes every hold.
verify: Record 30 repetitions; ensure no zero-warning release and all delays stay within authored bounds.

title: Staged rotation cap
requirement: Early/late/active/recovery stages enforce per-move turn limits.
behavior: Positioning can make a committed leap or spear charge pass the player, creating rear-flank punish windows; exact turn-rate curves remain unverified.
design: Use explicit early/late wind-up tracking, release lock and limited recovery-turn rates on each move; never 180-degree auto-snap mid strike.
verify: Circle behind during wind-up and after commit; plot yaw per stage and test dodge consistency.

title: Exclusive motion authority
requirement: Navigation/manual movement stops while root-motion/warp attack owns motion.
behavior: Dashes, leaps and cartwheels are visible, but the game’s locomotion/root-motion ownership internals are unknown.
design: Suspend AI MoveTo/CharacterMovement steering while an attack owns root motion or Motion Warping; restore cleanly at exit.
verify: Start a lunge while AI is chasing; detect no Nav/RootMotion tug-of-war or foot sliding.

title: Bounded Motion Warping
requirement: Warp target updates only in an authorized early window and obeys translation/rotation/Z/path caps.
behavior: Morgott changes displacement across leaps and charges; it is not established whether or how Souls game internals use a UE-style motion-warp system.
design: For a UE imitation, restrict motion-warp target updates to early preparation, clamp reach and yaw and prevent collision crossing.
verify: Jump sideways after warp lock; attack should miss rather than unnaturally curve into target.

title: Notify-end independence
requirement: Blend-out, interruption and watchdog all close any window even if Notify End is skipped.
behavior: No external source establishes whether his hit windows rely on notify-end callbacks or fail-safe lifecycle logic.
design: On Montage End, blend-out, interruption, phase transition and watchdog, always force all hit windows closed.
verify: Skip Notify End in a test asset or interrupt on active frame; verify trace stops immediately.

title: MoveCard handoff
requirement: Every move records axes, scale/FPS, timing, displacement, sockets, warp, cues, cancels and branches.
behavior: Morgott’s distinctive armament and geometry imply each move needs different animation specifications; his own studio asset documentation is private.
design: Create MoveCard for each sword, dagger, hammer, spear, tail, rain and bloodflame action: FPS, startup, contacts, root motion, sockets, cues and branches.
verify: Content review rejects any active attack without its MoveCard and montage-based timing sheet.

title: Geometry fidelity
requirement: Collision family and volume match the visible thrust, sweep, slam, ring, lane or grab.
behavior: Morgott uses narrow sword/spear thrusts, broad spinning blade arcs, heavy hammer impacts, tail sweeps, falling blades, bloodflame trails and bloodflame grab.
design: Use separate hit-volume families matching visible geometry: moving sword capsule, spear lane, sweep volumes, impact sphere, rain blades, persistent flame and grab capture.
verify: Capture synchronized weapon/hitbox overlays; each visible threat corresponds to a plausible collision volume.

title: Swept temporal sampling
requirement: Weapon samples sweep previous-to-current positions during active windows.
behavior: Visible blades move rapidly; exact Elden Ring collision sampling strategy is not publicly documented.
design: During active animation frames sweep each weapon sample from previous to current world transform rather than relying only on instantaneous overlap.
verify: Test 30 FPS, 120 FPS and deliberate frame spikes; a blade passing through a target registers once.

title: Blade interior samples
requirement: Long rotating weapons sample multiple points, not endpoints only.
behavior: Long sweeping weapon arcs would benefit from interior sampling; public observation does not prove internal sample count.
design: Add blade base, mid and tip samples (or contact segments) to the sword and spectral spear to cover interior trajectory.
verify: Put small test capsules at multiple places along blade; all should produce consistent contact.

title: Adaptive substeps
requirement: Excessive sample translation/angular delta creates bounded substeps.
behavior: Adaptive weapon trace subdivision is an engineering proposal, not a verified Morgott mechanic.
design: If angular or positional delta between frames exceeds budget, subdivide swept segments with a strict maximum work cap.
verify: Inject 100 ms frame hitch into fast spin attack; compare missed hit count and CPU cost.

title: Query filtering
requirement: Traces ignore owner/allies and use query-only channels with valid target/team checks.
behavior: The boss attacks opponents rather than itself, but underlying object channels and filters are unavailable.
design: Ignore attacker, attached weapon, friendly allied actors and non-targetables; use query-only physics channels and target classification.
verify: Spawn ally, summon and destructible prop between sword and target; verify correct candidates only.

title: Logical-victim dedupe
requirement: Multiple components/bones of one actor count once according to hit policy.
behavior: An ordinary sword swing should not multiply damage because it intersects multiple player bones; dedupe internals not visible.
design: Key hit victims by logical actor/character and attack-window ID, not individual mesh primitive or bone.
verify: Hit multiple skeletal bodies with one sweep; exactly one configured contact is applied.

title: Explicit hit policy
requirement: Once-per-attack, once-per-window, periodic and impact-plus-splash policies behave distinctly.
behavior: Multi-weapon strings contain separate strikes; holy sword rain and bloodflame ground effects can produce distinct successive hazards.
design: Define policy per attack window: once per strike, per impact, per projectile, periodic hazard, or separately flagged direct/splash.
verify: Stand in same AoE; verify hit frequency and knockback match each attack card.

title: Central defense order
requirement: Validity/dedupe, iframe, parry, guard, posture/armor, health and feedback resolve in one documented order.
behavior: Morgott’s fight supports dodge iframes, blocking, guard-break reactions and parryable physical sword attacks; internal resolution order is private.
design: Centralize defense resolution: valid target -> dedupe -> iframe -> parry -> guard -> armor/stance -> health -> feedback, with per-attack exceptions.
verify: Use same target in sword/spear/hammer/rain trials while blocking, dodging and parrying; record consistent rule application.

title: Iframe completeness
requirement: An invulnerable contact applies neither unintended health nor posture effects.
behavior: Well-timed rolls can avoid sword, hammer, spear and many AoE hits; exact secondary posture handling requires engine-level inspection.
design: When iframe succeeds, reject health, status and stance effects unless design explicitly says otherwise; handle undodgeable lingering mechanics separately.
verify: Roll through two contact windows and verify both direct and secondary effects behave per attack specification.

title: Direct/splash precedence
requirement: Direct and AoE overlap cannot double-dip unless the data explicitly permits it.
behavior: A hammer slam, bloodflame trail or geyser can overlap with its originating weapon impact; visible footage does not reveal dedupe policy.
design: Tag direct strike and splash actor with one logical AttackID; designate direct-hit priority and explicitly permit independent secondary explosion only when intended.
verify: Stand at impact center vs nearby ring; verify no accidental direct+splash double damage.

title: Swept annulus
requirement: Radial waves test the previous-to-current radius band and damage each victim once.
behavior: Morgott’s phase transition spawns localized eruptions/geysers, and holy rain occupies targeted lanes; it is not one uniform continuously expanding ring.
design: For the transition use timed geyser zones/overlap volumes; implement swept annulus only if a separate shockwave move explicitly needs an outward ring.
verify: Map impact zones and timing across the arena; ensure no invisible damage band or frame-step gap.

title: Grab fail-safe
requirement: Grab capture, defense, alignment, control lock, damage and release are explicit and restore on interrupt/death.
behavior: Phase-two Bloodflame Skewer/Grab impales a struck player, lifts them and throws them; it requires an authored capture/release lifecycle.
design: Implement capture validity, iframe/guard behavior, paired attacker-victim Montages, motion alignment, damage event, interruption/death release and control restoration.
verify: Interrupt the grab at startup, after capture, during lift, and at death; player always regains control.

title: Range-band policy
requirement: Close, ideal, approach and reacquire bands produce distinct movement/action preferences.
behavior: Morgott alternates close sword pressure, midrange spear threat and long-range dagger/spear actions; the player can influence his available moves through spacing.
design: Define close, ideal, chase and reacquire bands and choose movement based on the attack families available in each.
verify: Hold target at 1, 3, 7 and 12 meters; log qualitatively different movement and legal attack sets.

title: Combat positioning
requirement: Candidate positions score reachability, distance, LOS, wall/hazard clearance, flank and variety.
behavior: Morgott performs hops, sidesteps, cartwheels, approach and retreat; whether he uses numerical candidate-position scoring is unknown.
design: For UE, evaluate few reachable strafe/reposition points for distance, visibility, wall clearance and follow-up opportunities.
verify: Test backpedaling and wall proximity; boss chooses reachable non-clipping approach/reposition destinations.

title: Movement commitment
requirement: Strafe/approach choices have minimum duration and are not restarted every frame.
behavior: Movement feels deliberate, but there is no evidence of internal minimum commitment timers.
design: Give strafe/retreat choices minimum dwell time and interruption reasons, avoiding per-tick path change oscillation.
verify: Record move requests under moving target; no rapidly flipping left/right direction.

title: Wall-safe attacks
requirement: Root-motion/warp paths predict walls and use correction, fallback or decline.
behavior: Players report awkward fight patterns near the arena perimeter; leap and charge moves may be constrained by wall geometry.
design: Predict root-motion path sweep; decline or adjust risky attacks near walls rather than letting the capsule clip into arena props.
verify: Bait spear charge against walls at all headings and review penetration and animation displacement.

title: Arena-valid responses
requirement: Unreachable/elevated/outside targets cause reposition, search, leash or reset.
behavior: The shipped encounter uses a bounded arena, but elevated/outside/leash target response policy is not known.
design: If unreachable, fall back to seek, face, reacquire or reset; never throw a melee-only move at a target outside navmesh.
verify: Teleport test player beyond arena, above floor and behind blockers; boss exits invalid attack loop safely.

title: Arena/attack fit
requirement: Escape requirements and camera visibility are valid from every legal arena position.
behavior: The open Elden Throne arena supports lateral dodging and sightlines; holy swords rain creates lanes that constrain usable paths.
design: Ensure every attack has dodge paths from legal arena positions and camera can show weapon release; avoid spawning impossible hazard overlaps.
verify: Spawn player at center and every edge point; capture dodge-space coverage for rain, hammer and geysers.

title: Explicit attack segments
requirement: Every move declares anticipation, hold, commit, active, follow-through, recovery and neutral boundaries as applicable.
behavior: Morgott shows dramatic anticipation, fast active slashes, chained follow-through and enders with identifiable recovery; exact timeline boundaries require frame study.
design: For each MoveCard annotate anticipation, delayed hold, last tracking frame, active sub-windows, combo gate, recovery and neutral unlock.
verify: Export montage timeline for 12+ representative moves and compare to capture at slow playback.

title: Pressure variation
requirement: Offense rises and falls; neutral/recovery periodically reset pressure.
behavior: Sequences alternate explosive multi-hit offense, slow overhead anticipation, repositioning, and recognizable windows after specific enders.
design: Manage combo-pressure budget, slow/heavy versus fast attacks, and neutral reset probabilities without forcing unnatural pauses.
verify: Chart 20 consecutive fights: longest unbroken pressure, waits and punish frequency must meet authored combat targets.

title: Guaranteed openings
requirement: Some high-commitment moves have unconditionally meaningful recovery.
behavior: Players can punish holy sword rain setup, helicopter finisher, missed spear charge and many bloodflame enders; safety depends on position and weapon speed.
design: Mark actual guaranteed opening only after proving a chosen player weapon can start and exit safely from a defined position.
verify: For each claimed guaranteed opening, test light/heavy from close and flank distances with 30/60 FPS.

title: Conditional opening cues
requirement: Follow-up-capable recoveries reveal the gate/outcome consistently.
behavior: A hammer or sword continuation can be conditional on where the player rolls, so an apparent gap may not be a safe ender.
design: Make potential follow-up readable via animation stance, armament spawn, pause or audible cue; separate conditional recovery from true ender.
verify: Test players blind: can they recognize whether the boss has a pending branch?

title: Punish-margin calculation
requirement: Opening classification includes travel, player startup and safety buffer, not montage recovery alone.
behavior: Morgott’s openings depend strongly on dodge destination and weapon speed; a single recovery-animation length cannot describe punish safety.
design: Compute usable window = boss lock remaining − player approach − player attack startup − safety margin, for position/weapon variants.
verify: Measure actual travel/startup for light, heavy and flask; label guaranteed/conditional based on empirical margin.

title: Neutral is purposeful
requirement: Non-attacking time may face, strafe, observe or reset without hidden damage pressure.
behavior: Morgott may hop away, move, watch, or approach between strings; these intervals change positioning and open small decisions for the player.
design: Create neutral states with visible facing/footwork and bounded pacing controls; never allow invisible damage during neutral.
verify: Measure idle durations and confirm no hidden active traces between attacks.

title: Separate health/reaction/posture
requirement: Health, immediate flinch and posture accumulation have independent state and rules.
behavior: Morgott has health, staggerable attacks, and a separate stance/critical-opening system; successful parries also build toward a critical opening.
design: Separate health, one-hit reaction and cumulative stance resources; prevent incidental animation flinches from resetting stance unless authored.
verify: Compare chip damage, high-stagger attack and parry; confirm distinct health/reaction/posture outcomes.

title: Posture regeneration
requirement: Regeneration starts only after a documented quiet delay and rate, then resets correctly.
behavior: Community combat research reports a stance value of 80 and delayed reset behavior; exact patch-specific decay timing requires verification before treating it as a target.
design: Expose posture maximum, quiet timer and regeneration curve in boss data; tune to desired fight pacing rather than copying unseen internals.
verify: After a controlled stance hit, wait different delays and log posture regeneration transition.

title: Single stance break
requirement: Threshold produces one break, closes current offense and exposes a bounded critical window.
behavior: Once stance is depleted Morgott can fall into a critical-hit opportunity; parry chains also lead to riposte availability.
design: Fire stance break once at threshold, cancel offense, close active weapon windows and expose a timed critical socket state.
verify: Strike threshold during active combo and phase threshold; no duplicate breaks or stale active hit damage.

title: Windowed hyperarmor
requirement: Interruption resistance exists only for named moves/windows; health/posture policy is explicit.
behavior: Some moves are interruptible via stance pressure while others visibly continue through smaller hits; per-animation hyperarmor windows are not published.
design: Author hyperarmor windows per Montage section; specify effects on flinch and stance damage separately.
verify: Apply same stagger attack at startup, active and recovery for hammer, spear and bloodflame attacks.

title: Fair boss defense
requirement: Boss block/parry/dodge has facing/timing, startup, cooldown, cost and recovery constraints.
behavior: Morgott is not typically depicted using a shield-block/parry/dodge system like a humanoid duelist; his defensive repertoire is mainly repositioning, mobility and retaliatory threats.
design: Treat active boss block/parry as optional, not as a required copy of Morgott; if implemented, impose startup, angle, cooldown and recovery.
verify: Never claim this is a documented Morgott feature; prove fair reaction timings for any added defensive action.

title: Phase rule set
requirement: A phase defines move pool, utility modifiers, combo cap, movement, pressure, recovery and presentation.
behavior: Detailed moveset analysis describes an early sword-rain unlock around 80% HP, a dramatic cursed-blood transition around 60%, and an additional rapid armament barrage becoming eligible around 30%.
design: Represent threshold unlocks as data-driven event/phase flags; change attack pool, geyser hazard rule, pressure and follow-up families, not merely HP damage scale.
verify: Reduce HP slowly across thresholds; record first-time events, legal attacks before/after and late-fight move availability.

title: Safe transition policy
requirement: Threshold queues/delegates interruption according to one declared policy; first version should defer to a safe gate.
behavior: The transition visibly interrupts or supersedes current combat with sword-plant/cough and curse eruption; community analysis notes stagger can shift its actual activation point.
design: Queue one protected phase action at a documented safe/preemptive gate, cancel stale attack traces and do not transition into an invalid state.
verify: Cross threshold while staggered, grabbing and during combo branch; transition occurs once without stray damage.

title: Phase monotonicity
requirement: Healing and repeated threshold events do not oscillate or duplicate the transition.
behavior: Morgott does not visibly revert to an earlier move set after entering cursed-blood phase, and threshold events are one-time.
design: Monotonic phase state and one-shot transition flags; heals cannot rearm 80/60/30% unlock events.
verify: Artificially heal boss above a prior threshold; verify no duplicated sword-rain intro or phase transition.

title: Fair heal punish
requirement: Heal reaction requires committed heal, latency, LOS, range, travel feasibility, cooldown and free executor.
behavior: Healing or lengthy casts at vulnerable distances can provoke fast ranged or advancing pressure, but he is not guaranteed to react every time.
design: Only consider committed flask/cast after observable startup; add positive latency, LOS, range, travel and cooldown, and defer until executor free.
verify: Test instant/long heal at each range with and without LOS and while boss is mid-combo; report probabilities.

title: Anti-cheese with counterplay
requirement: Kiting, rear camping, guard, terrain and wall traps receive bounded readable responses or reset.
behavior: Tail whip addresses rear positioning; spears/daggers address distance; rain and geysers reshape arena movement, giving counterplay for overly safe habits.
design: Use bounded, telegraphed counters to rear camping, kiting, repeated guard and terrain abuse; never auto-correct strike trajectory into player.
verify: Repeat each exploit attempt 20 times; counters must be visible, avoidable and not force an infinite punish chain.

title: Runtime overlay
requirement: Debug view exposes phase/state/instance/context/attack/montage/tracking/window/gate/cooldown/pressure.
section: Debugging, QA, presentation and optional networking
behavior: Morgott’s actual game does not expose a developer overlay of combat state to players.
design: Add optional debug HUD of target distance, sector, phase flags, attack instance, montage, active hit windows, cooldowns and recovery.
verify: During fights compare HUD values against ground truth traces and events.

title: Structured event log
requirement: Decisions, commits, windows, contacts, defenses, branches, interrupts and transitions use stable IDs/times.
section: Debugging, QA, presentation and optional networking
behavior: No public structured runtime event log reveals private AI state.
design: Emit event logs keyed by encounter/attack/branch ID with monotonic timestamps, contextual inputs, collision hits and aborts.
verify: Correlate a single multi-hit string from selection to attack end across serverless runtime logs.

title: Reproducible scenarios
requirement: Seed, starts, player script, time, phase and IDs are recorded.
section: Debugging, QA, presentation and optional networking
behavior: Player recordings can show repeated fight patterns, but they are not deterministic seeds of FromSoftware AI.
design: Record seeded decision RNG, player replay scripts, starting phase/position, cooldowns and version; support deterministic automation trials.
verify: Replay same scripted player trajectory twice and compare selected action sequence.

title: FPS and time-scale parity
requirement: 30/60/120 FPS and supported time scales do not change hit count, cleanup or legal decisions.
section: Debugging, QA, presentation and optional networking
behavior: No reliable public test proves Morgott’s internal 30/60/120 FPS parity or time-dilation safety.
design: Run frame-rate capped automated cases for charge, sweep, grab, rain, phase transition and stance break; compare hit counts and decision legality.
verify: Execute 30/60/120 FPS plus induced hitch; no unjustified duplicate/missed damage or orphaned state.

title: Performance bounds
requirement: Utility is gate-driven; traces run only while active with bounded samples; packaged frame cost is profiled.
section: Debugging, QA, presentation and optional networking
behavior: Exact CPU cost of Morgott’s combat decision evaluator and collision system is not public.
design: Evaluate utility at events, not every tick; trace only while hit active; bounded substeps and pooled projectile/hazard effects.
verify: Unreal Insights packaged runs across low/high frame settings and demanding Phase 2 hazards.

title: Camera/readability
requirement: Boss target point, camera collision and framing keep release cues/weapon threats visible.
section: Debugging, QA, presentation and optional networking
behavior: Long weapon swings and overhead attacks require readable camera framing; even this polished encounter can sometimes crowd the camera at close range.
design: Ensure lock-on point, camera collision and arena edge positioning keep release cues in frame; adjust own boss scale and effects as needed.
verify: Capture camera from 8 compass bearings at near/far distances during huge hammer and bloodflame effects.

title: Accessible feedback
requirement: Shake/effect reduction and non-color-only audiovisual cues preserve attack distinctions.
section: Debugging, QA, presentation and optional networking
behavior: Accessibility settings and non-color-only cue completeness cannot be inferred from Morgott gameplay guides alone.
design: Provide distinctive poses/audio/shape cues separate from holy-gold vs blood-red colors, with optional camera-shake/effect reductions.
verify: Test color-blind filters, low VFX, no audio and constrained camera; moves remain distinguishable.
